{{Quote|So you thought you could hide your deal with the offworlders from me, droid? I'm tired of not getting my cut!|Ganga Lor, to Switch|<ref name="TTD" />}}
'''Switch''' was a [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] who worked as both a [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] and an [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]] on the [[XQ2 Platform]] [[Sel Zonn Station]] in the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] following the [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|end]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Switch established a [[Switch's organization|criminal organization]] that was based in a [[Deep Storage Bay V14|storage bay]] on Sel Zonn Station. He soon became a rival of the [[Chevin/Legends|Chevin]] criminal [[Ganga Lor]], and he competed with Lor for control of illegal activities aboard the [[Space station/Legends|space station]].

In about [[17 BBY/Legends|17 BBY]], Switch was hired by [[Alderaanian Security]] to collect and receive one of [[Unidentified Alderaanian Security agent|their agents]], who had been [[Carbon-freezing/Legends|frozen]] in a slab of [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] while on an assignment in the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]]. The protocol [[Droid/Legends|droid]] gained possession of the frozen operative, and the [[Alderaanian/Legends|Alderaanian]] Security [[Agent/Legends|agent]] [[Maya]] was dispatched to collect the carbonite slab from Switch. After Maya was attacked by [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], a group of [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] met with Switch in her place, and they negotiated with him for the frozen agent's release. However, just as Switch and the spacers concluded their business, they were attacked by Ganga Lor and a group of his thugs. Switch and the spacers defeated the Chevin, and, shortly afterward, the spacers traveled to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]] on a mission for the [[Alderaanian Resistance]], a rebellious movement led by [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]]. A [[TC-663|contact]] working for Switch obtained copies of some encrypted messages that had been sent from the [[Darga the Hutt's palace|palace]] of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Darga Jiramma Mionne|Darga]] on Cato Neimoidia, and Switch ordered his contact to make the messages available to the spacers. Switch later sent the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Koroma Moro]] to compete in the [[Cloud City Sabacc Tournament]] on the planet [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]], and the droid engaged the assistance of the spacers to ensure that Moro won the competition.

==Biography==
===Arrival on Sel Zonn Station===
[[File:DeepStorage_Bay_V14.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Deep Storage Bay V14, the area from where Switch ran his organization]]
Switch was a [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] who,<ref name="TTD" /> at some point prior to [[17 BBY/Legends|17 BBY]],<ref name="Date">The ''[[Dawn of Defiance]]'' module ''[[Echoes of the Jedi]]'' states that the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Vhiin Thorla]] traveled to the [[Almas Academy]] two years after the declaration of [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]], which is dated to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. Thus this indicates that ''Dawn of Defiance'' is set in circa 17 BBY.</ref> set himself up as an [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]] and [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] on [[Sel Zonn Station]], an [[XQ2 Platform]] that [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal IV]]. He founded a [[Switch's organization|criminal organization]] and assembled a group of [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] thugs to work for him, as well as hiring a [[Unidentified Twi'lek majordomo (Sel Zonn Station)|Twi'lek]] to serve as his [[Majordomo/Legends|majordomo]], and engaging the services of the [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R5-B8]]. Switch established a base of operations for himself in [[Deep Storage Bay V14]], on a level of the [[Space station/Legends|station]] that had restricted access.<ref name="TTD" />

Although he soon became well-known on the station, Switch was able to keep the location of his headquarters secret from most of the inhabitants of Sel Zonn Station, because V14 was quarantined due to some exhaust conduits that passed through the bay. To further ensure that Switch's use of V14 remained secret, the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] had his majordomo bring [[Standard month/Legends|monthly]] bribes to the [[Unidentified Sel Zonn Station manager|station's manager]], to ensure that the bay remained off-limits. He allowed the bay to fall into disrepair and had an expensive [[japor ivory wood]] desk placed in the center of the room from which he conducted his business. The protocol droid soon gained a rival in the form of [[Ganga Lor]], a [[Chevin/Legends|Chevin]] crime [[Lord/Legends|lord]] who had arrived on the station at about the same [[Time/Legends|time]] as him. Switch also had some dealings with the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Byra Fenn]], the operator of the pharmaceutical supplier [[Delgas Medical Supplies]], and she owed him some favors as a result.<ref name="TTD" />

===Business with the Alderaanian rebels===
{{Quote|Turn him into scrap, boys!|Ganga Lor, ordering his thugs to attack Switch|<ref name="TTD" />}}
Circa 17 BBY,<ref name="Date" /> Switch was hired by [[Alderaanian Security]], a security force from the planet [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], to collect and store some cargo for them, which contained one of [[Unidentified Alderaanian Security agent|their agents]]. The [[Agent/Legends|agent]] was returning from an assignment [[Spy/Legends|spying]] on the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]], and had been [[Carbon-freezing/Legends|frozen]] in a slab of [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] to reduce the chance of capture by the Empire while traveling back to Alderaan. Switch arranged for the cargo to arrive on Sel Zonn Station in a cargo bay on [[Blue Deck]], an Imperial-controlled zone of the station, as he believed that the Imperials would not expect anyone to be bold enough to hide contraband there. However, Ganga Lor became jealous of Switch's deal with the [[Alderaanian/Legends|Alderaanians]], and the Chevin began plotting to rid himself of his rival. Around that time, Switch was also contracted to arrange for a crate of [[Corellian ale/Legends|Corellian ale]] to be delivered to an address on Alderaan, and he stored the [[Ale/Legends|ale]] in the Blue Deck cargo bay with the carbonite-frozen Alderaanian.<ref name="TTD" />

An Alderaanian agent called [[Maya]] was sent by [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] to collect the frozen operative from Switch, but she was attacked by [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] soon after arriving on Sel Zonn Station. A group of [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] who attempted to help her escape from the Imperials found out about the cargo, so they went to collect the carbonite slab from Switch in Maya's place. On their arrival at Switch's cargo bay, the protocol droid introduced himself and R5-B8 to the agents and offered them drinks from his extensive collection. The spacers entered negotiations with him for the release of the frozen Alderaanian, and he offered to release the cargo in return for a payment of 1,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]. However, just as the spacers were concluding their business with the protocol droid, Ganga Lor and a group of Lor's thugs entered the room and attacked Switch and the spacers. Even though Lor had bribed Switch's own thugs prior to the attack, so that they would not fight hard, Switch and the spacers were able to [[Death/Legends|kill]] the Chevin [[Gangster/Legends|gangster]] and all of his cronies. Lor's [[Ganga Lor's organization|organization]] was destroyed, because all of his men had participated in the attack, so the Chevin's demise allowed Switch to gain greater control over crime on Sel Zonn Station.<ref name="TTD" />

A short time afterward, Switch received some information from [[TC-663]], a protocol droid contact of his who worked on the planet [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]] as a [[Translator/Legends|translator]] for the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] crime lord [[Darga Jiramma Mionne]]. Darga's [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] majordomo, [[Igren Demos]], had secretly sent a number of messages to the Imperial [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitor]] [[Valin Draco]] while the Hutt [[Sleep/Legends|slept]], and through monitoring communications from [[Darga the Hutt's palace|Darga's palace]] TC-663 had realized that one of Darga's associates was dealing with the Empire without the Hutt's knowledge. The translator sent copies of Demos' messages to Switch, but the information broker was unable to break their encryption. The spacers Switch had encountered on Sel Zonn Station had since joined the [[Alderaanian Resistance]], an anti-Imperial rebellious movement led by Senator Organa, and were staying as guests at Darga's palace, so Switch ordered TC-663 to give the spacers a copy of the transmissions. Switch hoped that the spacers would be able to break the encryption and would share the information from the messages with TC-663, who could then send the intelligence onto Switch on Sel Zonn Station.<ref name="AWH">{{DoD|A Wretched Hive (adventure)}}</ref>

===Fixing the Cloud City Sabacc Tournament===
Darga relocated to [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] on the planet [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] after the Alderaanian Resistance agents released the captive [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Denia]] from Darga's palace, and the Resistance team subsequently traveled to Cloud City in search of the Hutt. Some of Switch's contacts in the [[City/Legends|city]] informed him that they had sighted the agents there, and the protocol droid developed a plan to work with the agents to ensure that a victor of Switch's choice won the upcoming [[Cloud City Sabacc Tournament]]. At Switch's behest, the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Koroma Moro]], a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Captain/Legends|captain]] who had hauled shipments of cargo for Switch in the past, signed up for the competition, with an entry fee supplied by Switch. The droid then set up a means by which the Alderaanian Resistance agents could contact him via Cloud City's communications system, and he sent a message to Captain [[Sirona Okeefe]] of the Resistance, requesting that the agents get in touch with him.<ref name="TQOAAD">{{DoD|The Queen of Air and Darkness}}</ref>

{{RPG|"[[The Queen of Air and Darkness]]"}}
The agents contacted Switch and accepted his proposal, and the droid offered them five percent of the competition winnings if Moro won the tournament. The Twi'lek performed well during the opening stages of the competition, and, three [[Standard day/Legends|days]] into the event, Switch sent the agents a piece of software that he intended for them to install into the tournament's [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] [[Dealer droid/Legends|dealer droids]] to alter the droids' programming and turn the odds of the competition in Moro's favor. The agents installed the program, and, as a result, Moro won the competition.<ref name="TQOAAD" />
{{Endgame}}

==Characteristics==
By the time he became an information broker, Switch had not had a [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipe]] for a long while, which allowed him to develop a greater degree of individuality than most droids. The remnants of his protocol droid programming led him to have aspirations of sophistication, and, to demonstrate his refined tastes, he acquired an extensive collection of beverages and a rare, hand-crafted Japor ivory wood desk. Switch spoke with a [[Coruscanti/Legends|Coruscanti]]-Imperial accent and enunciated himself like an upper-class Human, making him sound as urbane as he tried to appear. However, while he spoke cheerily and lightly, he was not as civilized or friendly as he tried to present himself; he gave no value to life and thought nothing of the deaths of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings. Despite his impassiveness, Switch understood the concept of friendship and considered R5-B8 to be his most valued companion. He was persuasive and possessed good criminal acumen, and it was these traits that he used to form his organization and convince the sentient beings who served him to make him their leader.<ref name="TTD" /> He had an interest in illicit activities that took place throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]],<ref name="TQOAAD" /> and he made his services available to anyone who was prepared to pay for them. He also liked to flicker his [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]] to imitate blinking.<ref name="TTD" />

Switch was covered in shiny, ebony-[[Color/Legends|colored]] plating and was fitted with standard protocol droid systems, including a processor, a [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulator]], a [[Electronic translator|translation unit]], and hand [[Limb/Legends|appendages]]. He also carried with him an [[Recorder|audio recorder]], a [[Hold-out blaster/Legends|hold-out blaster]], a [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]], and a [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]].<ref name="TTD" />

==Behind the scenes==
Switch was created by [[Rodney Thompson]] and appeared in ''[[The Traitor's Gambit]]'', the first adventure in the ''[[Dawn of Defiance]]'' [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game|roleplaying]] campaign.<ref name="TTD" /> He later received mentions in [[A Wretched Hive (adventure)|''A Wretched Hive'']] and ''[[The Queen of Air and Darkness]]'', the second and third installments of the campaign, which were also written by Thompson.<ref name="AWH" /><ref name="TQOAAD" /> In ''The Traitor's Gambit'', the players [[Roleplaying game|roleplay]] as the group of spacers who negotiate with Switch for the release of the frozen Alderaanian, and when the player characters first arrive at Switch's cargo bay, it is possible for them to engage in a fight with Switch's Gamorrean [[Bodyguard/Legends|guards]]. If they choose to do so, Switch is not bothered by the fight. The players also have a variety of options for how their negotiations with Switch can occur, and they can persuade him to reduce his fee by 200 credits if they agree to supply him with information on a regular basis. They can also bribe him to find out about the nature of cargo that they are collecting, and if they mention that they own a starship, Switch offers to pay them to deliver a crate of Corellian ale to an address on Alderaan.<ref name="TTD" />

If the players fail to persuade Switch to tell them the cargo's location, he gives it to them after the conclusion of Ganga Lor's attack. If any of the player characters are injured during the fight, Switch calls in a favor with Byra Fenn to get the spacers healed free of charge. It is also possible for Switch to be destroyed during the attack,<ref name="TTD" /> but this outcome is presumably [[Canon|non-canon]], because ''A Wretched Hive'' and ''The Queen of Air and Darkness'' indicate that he was active after the attack.<ref name="AWH" /><ref name="TQOAAD" /> Once the spacers' business with Switch is concluded, it is possible for the droid to contact Sirona Okeefe and tell her that the spacers require [[Transport/Legends|transport]] off the station.<ref name="TTD" />

In ''The Queen of Air and Darkness'', Switch requests that the player characters help him to ensure that Koroma Mora wins the Cloud City Sabacc Tournament, and the players have the option of either accepting or rejecting the request. If the players agree to help Switch, the droid initially offers them five percent of Moro's winnings, and if the players choose to negotiate with him, they can persuade Switch to offer them up to seven percent of the prize money. During the competition, if the player characters fail to tell Moro that they are working for Switch, the protocol droid sends Moro a message that informs him that the agents will be providing him assistance. It is then later possible for Moro to win the tournament.<ref name="TQOAAD" />
